questions.prompt: What did Festinger, Schachter, and Back set out to study in the MIT complexes?
questions.promptZh: Festinger、Schachter 与 Back 在 MIT 住宅群中研究什么？
options: How every resident's marriage ended in divorce.
The formation of friendships in relation to distance.
Which students obtained the highest examination marks.
The population growth of Philadelphia in 1931 alone.
optionsZh: 每个居民的婚姻如何离婚结束。
与距离相关的友谊形成。
哪些学生考试分最高。
仅1931年费城人口增长。
analyses: A friendship formation 不是全部婚姻结局。
B distance and relationships、examine friendship formation 两项明确，地点为 Westgate 与 Westgate West。
C 无成绩测验。
D 这是1940年代末 MIT 住宅环境研究，不能混成前面的费城婚姻资料；未限定全是本科生或补入未述身份。

vocabulary.meaning: 着手；以做某事为目标开始
vocabulary.context: 说明研究目标，不是说先前已证明全部机制。
vocabulary.example: The team set out to examine how shared spaces affected meetings.
collocations: set out to examine friendship formation

questions.evidenceQuote: In the late 1940s, social psychologists Leon Festinger, Stan Schachter, and Kurt Back were also interested in distance and relationships when they set out to examine friendship formation in two MIT residential complexes: Westgate and Westgate West. Unlike the city of Philadelphia, there were no ethnic enclaves—no Chinatown where Chinese immigrants would gravitate, for example—so the selection effect (i.e., a resident choosing to live in a particular area) was kept to a minimum.

questions.prompt: What were residents asked to name in the study?
questions.promptZh: 研究要求居民说出什么？
options: Every person they had ever married.
The three units with the largest rooms.
The three people in the complexes whom they saw most socially.
The three geographically farthest strangers they had never met.
optionsZh: 所有曾结婚对象。
面积最大的三个单元。
在住宅群中社交见得最多的三个人。
从未见过且地理最远的三个陌生人。
analyses: A 当前是社交提名，不是婚史调查。
B three people 不是房间面积或单元排名。
C 问句 what three people...see most of socially 明确对象及社交标准。
D 见得最多不能换成从没见过；居民地址已知用于分析距离，不是要求只报最远者。

vocabulary.meaning: 在社交上；作为交往接触地
vocabulary.context: 界定谁最常见，不等于仅工作通信、家族血缘或恋爱关系。
vocabulary.example: The residents reported whom they saw most often socially.

questions.evidenceQuote: Festinger and colleagues knew exactly where all the participants in this study lived, and asked one simple question: “What three people in Westgate or Westgate West do you see most of socially?” In the microcosm of a college dorm, their research replicated the Philadelphia and Dutch findings: 112 out of the possible 187 friendship nominations, or 60 percent, lived next door or in the unit connected directly through staircases. Only seven nominations were made of someone living four units away or more. So, physical distance clearly matters.

questions.prompt: What does the number seven refer to in the nomination finding?
questions.promptZh: 提名结果里的 seven 指什么？
options: Nominations of someone living four units away or more.
The total number of all residents in both complexes.
Seven percent of every possible marriage in Philadelphia.
The number of staircases every participant had to climb.
optionsZh: 提名相距四个单元或更远者的次数。
两住宅群全部居民总数。
费城每种可能婚姻的7%。
每人必须爬的楼梯数。
analyses: A seven nominations、four units away or more 是计数与距离类别对应。
B 不是居民总人数。
C seven 为次数非7%，也非费城婚姻。
D 楼梯与功能接近有关，但此数字不计楼梯；不把同一人的多次提名必当独立夫妻对。

vocabulary.meaning: 提名；受试者指认的社交对象记录
vocabulary.context: 不同于独立居民总数或婚姻数量，统计单位不能互换。
vocabulary.example: The survey recorded nominations of frequent social contacts.

questions.evidenceQuote: Festinger and colleagues knew exactly where all the participants in this study lived, and asked one simple question: “What three people in Westgate or Westgate West do you see most of socially?” In the microcosm of a college dorm, their research replicated the Philadelphia and Dutch findings: 112 out of the possible 187 friendship nominations, or 60 percent, lived next door or in the unit connected directly through staircases. Only seven nominations were made of someone living four units away or more. So, physical distance clearly matters.

questions.prompt: What does 'So, physical distance clearly matters' do after the numbers?
questions.promptZh: 数字之后 So,physical distance clearly matters 做什么？
options: It denies any relation between residence and social contact.
It proves physical distance is the sole sufficient cause of every friendship.
It starts a new experiment that measures no relationships.
It draws the author's conclusion from the reported pattern of nearby nominations.
optionsZh: 否认住址与交往有任何联系。
证明物理距离是每段友谊唯一充分原因。
开始不测关系的新实验。
根据近处提名模式得出作者结论。
analyses: A So 接总结而非否认。
B matters 不等于 only cause，也不保证住得近必为朋友。
C 无新样本或新方法。
D 近邻或楼梯直接连通多、四单元外少，支持作者所述重要性；不要将该句独自当排除了所有其他因素的随机因果证明。

vocabulary.meaning: 重要；起作用
vocabulary.context: 在结论中说明值得考虑的影响，不是唯一决定一切，也非名词事件。
vocabulary.example: The pattern suggests that opportunities for contact matter.

questions.evidenceQuote: Festinger and colleagues knew exactly where all the participants in this study lived, and asked one simple question: “What three people in Westgate or Westgate West do you see most of socially?” In the microcosm of a college dorm, their research replicated the Philadelphia and Dutch findings: 112 out of the possible 187 friendship nominations, or 60 percent, lived next door or in the unit connected directly through staircases. Only seven nominations were made of someone living four units away or more. So, physical distance clearly matters.

questions.prompt: What does 'functional distance' add beyond simple physical distance?
questions.promptZh: functional distance 比简单物理距离多强调什么？
options: How routes such as staircases affect opportunities to meet across floors.
Only the straight-line number of metres, with all routes irrelevant.
The official ranking of a resident's job function.
A guarantee that every pair on different floors never becomes friends.
optionsZh: 楼梯等通行路线怎样影响跨楼层见面机会。
只有直线米数，路线全无关。
居民职业职能的官方排名。
保证不同楼层者绝不会成朋友。
analyses: A 住楼梯近者更可能跨层交友，体现实际通行造成的功能接近。
B also matters 与楼梯比较不支持完全无关。
C function 不是职业排名。
D far more likely 指不同机会，不是不同楼层绝无友谊；概率增加不等于每次会面必成友。

vocabulary.meaning: 功能距离；实际通行与遇见机会造成的接近程度
vocabulary.context: 区别单纯直线距离，关注路线如何让人更易碰面。
vocabulary.example: The staircase reduced functional distance between residents on different floors.

questions.evidenceQuote: The other interesting finding from the study was that functional distance also matters. Those who lived close to the staircases were far more likely to become friends with someone living on a different floor than those who lived farther away from the staircases. What this suggests is that physical and functional distance dictate the probability of a chance meeting, and that the more frequently one meets someone informally, the more likely it is that a friendship emerges.

questions.prompt: What do repeated chance meetings increase in the stated explanation?
questions.promptZh: 所述解释中，反复偶遇增加什么？
options: A guarantee that everyone shares identical objective traits.
The physical length of the residence corridor.
Familiarity.
The number of countries recorded in the marriage study.
optionsZh: 所有人客观特质相同的保证。
住宅走廊实体长度。
熟悉感。
婚姻研究记录的国家数。
analyses: A familiarity 不是客观性格相同。
B 不会由会面本身增加走廊长度。
C What repeated chance meetings do is increase familiarity 直接对应，后面引入实验。
D 不是国家数；当前机制解释也不意味着每个熟悉对象都必受喜爱。

vocabulary.meaning: 熟悉感；因多次接触而不陌生的程度
vocabulary.context: 不同于已确认事实知识、客观相似或真正建立深厚友谊。
vocabulary.example: Repeated encounters increased familiarity with the faces.

questions.evidenceQuote: At their best, social psychologists work by identifying an association between two variables in the real world (e.g., residential proximity and friendship), then test causal mechanisms, or what accounts for the observed correlation. What repeated chance meetings do is increase familiarity. Bob Zajonc, one of the greatest social psychologists of all time, zeroed in on the familiarity effect, or what he called the “mere exposure effect,” in a series of experiments.

questions.prompt: What did Zajonc 'zero in on' in the experiments described here?
questions.promptZh: 这里 Zajonc 的实验 zero in on 什么？
options: The mating choices of every Dutch resident.
The proximity of Philadelphia marriage-licence offices.
The relative salaries of secretaries after hiring.
The familiarity effect, also called the mere exposure effect.
optionsZh: 每位荷兰居民的择偶。
费城结婚许可办公室的邻近。
秘书聘后的相对薪资。
熟悉感效应，也称单纯曝光效应。
analyses: A 荷兰资料是前文不同研究。
B 不是办公室位置研究。
C 不属于秘书模型聘后工资任务。
D zeroed in on 指聚焦，后接 familiarity effect 与另称，非把效应缩成零。

vocabulary.meaning: 聚焦于；把注意力集中到
vocabulary.context: 不是降低为零或忽略，描述研究焦点。
vocabulary.example: The experiment zeroed in on the effect of repeated presentation.
collocations: zeroed in on the familiarity effect

questions.evidenceQuote: At their best, social psychologists work by identifying an association between two variables in the real world (e.g., residential proximity and friendship), then test causal mechanisms, or what accounts for the observed correlation. What repeated chance meetings do is increase familiarity. Bob Zajonc, one of the greatest social psychologists of all time, zeroed in on the familiarity effect, or what he called the “mere exposure effect,” in a series of experiments.

questions.prompt: When did Zajonc refine the earlier word-frequency research relative to this series of experiments?
questions.promptZh: 相对这一系列实验，Zajonc 何时改进早前词频研究？
options: Only after the classroom experiment had ended.
Before he conducted this series of experiments.
Only after collecting the Dutch cohabitation records.
At a time the passage explicitly says cannot be placed in order.
optionsZh: 仅课堂实验结束后。
在他开展这一系列实验之前。
仅收集荷兰同居记录之后。
段落明确说无法判顺序的时候。
analyses: A Even before 与 only after 相反。
B 开头 even before conducted this series 给出时序，refinement 对已有研究而言。
C 荷兰记录不在此研究时序中。
D 本句已明示先后，不是未给；不添加未述精确年份。

vocabulary.meaning: 改进；使既有方法或论证更精细
vocabulary.context: 不同于第一次凭空发明全部研究，也非结果已变因果定律。
vocabulary.example: The researcher proposed a refinement of the earlier comparison.

questions.evidenceQuote: Even before he conducted this series of experiments, Zajonc made an ingenious refinement of previous research on word frequency and its link to perceived “desirability” of a word (i.e., how good or bad a word sounds). Word frequency was measured by how often each word appeared in published books and magazines in the 1920s and 1930s, in painstaking work conducted by Edward Thorndike and Irving Lorge. Desirability was determined by aggregating English speakers’ ratings of various English words.

questions.prompt: How was word frequency measured in the earlier work?
questions.promptZh: 早先工作怎样测量词频？
options: By counting appearances in published books and magazines from the 1920s and 1930s.
Only by asking speakers which word sounded most pleasant.
By counting how often each participant attended the lecture.
By measuring how long a person took to pronounce a nonsense word once.
optionsZh: 数1920、1930年代出版书籍杂志中的出现次数。
只问哪个词最悦耳。
数每人上课次数。
测读一次无意义词所需时长。
analyses: A how often appeared、books/magazines、年代对应；计数工作归 Thorndike 与 Lorge。
B 那是讨喜程度评分，不是词频。
C 属后面的课堂曝光设计，不能挪来。
D 发音任务属于后续实验，且这里未测发音时长。

vocabulary.meaning: 细致费力的；不厌其烦的
vocabulary.context: 形容早期词频计数工作的投入，不是参与者感到身体痛。
vocabulary.example: The catalogue was the result of painstaking counting.

questions.evidenceQuote: Even before he conducted this series of experiments, Zajonc made an ingenious refinement of previous research on word frequency and its link to perceived “desirability” of a word (i.e., how good or bad a word sounds). Word frequency was measured by how often each word appeared in published books and magazines in the 1920s and 1930s, in painstaking work conducted by Edward Thorndike and Irving Lorge. Desirability was determined by aggregating English speakers’ ratings of various English words.

questions.prompt: What contrast does the opening comment about 'good' and 'better' prepare?
questions.promptZh: 关于 good 与 better 的开头评论为哪种对照作铺垫？
options: A rule that good is the grammatical comparative of better.
A finding that every English speaker always dislikes both words.
The difference between the words' comparative meaning and later frequency-related desirability ratings.
A claim that better occurs more often than good in the described counts.
optionsZh: good 是 better 比较级的语法规则。
每位英语使用者总讨厌两个词的发现。
词语比较意义与后面词频相关讨喜评分之间的区别。
所述计数中 better 比 good 更常见。
analyses: A 英语比较关系并非如此，当前也不把喜好评分改成语法规则。
B Everyone agrees 是作者行文开场，不是全英语人群厌恶测量。
C 通常语义 better 比 good 更好，与后面 good 因高频却更讨喜构成引人注意的反差。
D 下一句明确 good used far more often；保持词义、词频和主观评分三者分开。

vocabulary.meaning: 就……而言；从……方面看
vocabulary.context: 同段转到 word frequency 的评价维度，不把语义优劣当词频统计。
vocabulary.example: In terms of frequency, the shorter word appeared more often.
collocations: the word good is used far more often

questions.evidenceQuote: Everyone agrees that the word “good” is good, but not as good as the word “better.” But, in terms of word frequency, the word “good” is used far more often than the word “better.” So, if frequent encounters increase the desirability of a word, then the word “good” should be more desirable than the word “better.” Indeed, participants in a psychology experiment reported that the word “good” is more desirable than the word “better”!

questions.prompt: What status does the 'if ... then ... should' sentence give the claim about good's desirability?
questions.promptZh: if...then...should 句使 good 更讨喜处于什么性质？
options: A definition requiring every person to prefer good regardless of evidence.
A completed proof that frequency alone caused all English preferences.
An instruction to replace every use of better with good.
A conditional prediction derived from higher encounter frequency.
optionsZh: 不论证据都要求每人偏好 good 的定义。
已完成频率单独造成全部英语偏好的证明。
要求把所有 better 替换 good。
从较高接触频率推导的条件性预测。
analyses: A should 在预测中不是强制个人喜好。
B if 标记假设，后续原书还明确此词频证据仍相关性。
C 不是写作替换指令。
D 若多接触增讨喜，加上 good 更高频，就预测它评分更高；区别预测与因果已证。

vocabulary.meaning: 按假设推理应当会；预期会
vocabulary.context: 这里为预测而非道德命令，不能改成已在所有人中证实。
vocabulary.example: If the hypothesis is right, the repeated image should receive a higher rating.

questions.evidenceQuote: Everyone agrees that the word “good” is good, but not as good as the word “better.” But, in terms of word frequency, the word “good” is used far more often than the word “better.” So, if frequent encounters increase the desirability of a word, then the word “good” should be more desirable than the word “better.” Indeed, participants in a psychology experiment reported that the word “good” is more desirable than the word “better”!

questions.prompt: How does 'Indeed' connect the reported participant ratings to the preceding prediction?
questions.promptZh: Indeed 怎样把参与者评分与前面预测联系？
options: It introduces a finding that directly reverses the stated prediction.
It introduces reported ratings consistent with good being rated more desirable than better.
It changes better's grammatical meaning into worse.
It says no participant provided a rating.
optionsZh: 引入直接反转原预测的发现。
引入与 good 比 better 更讨喜相符的自报评分。
把 better 的语法意义改为 worse。
说没有参与者评分。
analyses: A reported good more desirable 与前句预测同向，非反转。
B Indeed 表果然，participants reported 是该评分结果；不等于改变单词的词典比较意义。
C 主观讨喜不是比较级语义改写。
D 原句明说 reported；这种相符也不能删掉后文对相关证据的因果限制。

vocabulary.meaning: 果然；的确（此处承接相符结果）
vocabulary.context: 连接预测和观察，不自动使全部证据成为因果实验。
vocabulary.example: The prediction favoured the repeated item; indeed, it received higher ratings.

questions.evidenceQuote: Everyone agrees that the word “good” is good, but not as good as the word “better.” But, in terms of word frequency, the word “good” is used far more often than the word “better.” So, if frequent encounters increase the desirability of a word, then the word “good” should be more desirable than the word “better.” Indeed, participants in a psychology experiment reported that the word “good” is more desirable than the word “better”!

questions.prompt: What limitation remains in the earlier word-frequency findings?
questions.promptZh: 早先词频发现还存在什么限制？
options: They are correlational and do not by themselves establish a causal effect of frequency on liking.
They prove that frequency can have no possible effect on liking.
They show every word has been presented an experimentally identical number of times.
They contain no observations or ratings of words at all.
optionsZh: 仍是相关性结果，不能单凭它确立频率对喜欢的因果。
证明频率绝不可能影响喜欢。
表明每个词都被实验呈现相同次数。
完全没有词语观察或评分。
analyses: A still correlational 后明确 cannot infer causal effect，区分有联系与因果已识别。
B 不能推因果不等于证明无效。
C 词频自然差别是先前资料，不是各词实验次数相同。
D 有计数与评分，局限不等于从无证据。

vocabulary.meaning: 推断；从证据得出结论
vocabulary.context: cannot infer 因果限定证据所能支持的强度，不是说研究毫无价值。
vocabulary.example: The pattern alone does not allow us to infer causation.

questions.evidenceQuote: The findings from this research on word frequency are fascinating, but they are still correlational. That is, we cannot infer a causal effect between frequency and liking a word. So Zajonc designed an experiment in which participants were presented with nonsense words such as “iktitaf,” “afworbu,” and “saricik.” The experimenter told the participants that these were “Turkish” words (they weren’t) and showed them how to pronounce each.

questions.prompt: How do the new materials differ from the earlier comparison of existing words?
questions.promptZh: 新材料与早先既有词比较有何区别？
options: They are verified translations of every English comparison word.
They are all selected from actual Turkish dictionaries with known meanings.
They introduce nonsense words in an experiment rather than relying only on existing word-frequency associations.
They replace repeated exposure with a study of marriage addresses.
optionsZh: 它们是每个英语比较词已核实的译文。
全选自真实土耳其词典且词义已知。
实验引入无意义词，而非只依靠既有词频关联。
以婚姻地址研究替代反复曝光。
analyses: A 不是给 good/better 一一翻译。
B 紧后 they weren’t 明确是假词，不是真实土耳其词表。
C So designed experiment...nonsense words 明确从相关结果转新实验。
D 并非地址研究；不自行添加未述随机化细节或每个假词真实释义。

vocabulary.meaning: 无意义词；实验中编造的词形
vocabulary.context: 此处不具备供学习的真实土耳其词义，不能写进词汇表当真实外语词。
vocabulary.example: The experiment used nonsense words to create unfamiliar stimuli.

questions.evidenceQuote: The findings from this research on word frequency are fascinating, but they are still correlational. That is, we cannot infer a causal effect between frequency and liking a word. So Zajonc designed an experiment in which participants were presented with nonsense words such as “iktitaf,” “afworbu,” and “saricik.” The experimenter told the participants that these were “Turkish” words (they weren’t) and showed them how to pronounce each.

questions.prompt: Why is the parenthesis 'they weren’t' important after 'Turkish' words?
questions.promptZh: Turkish words 后的 they weren’t 为何重要？
options: It says the participants were not human.
It distinguishes the experimenter's cover description from the words' actual status.
It proves the participants already knew genuine Turkish fluently.
It cancels the instruction that each pronunciation was demonstrated.
optionsZh: 说参与者不是人。
区别实验者的掩饰性说法与词的实际性质。
证明参与者已流利掌握真正土耳其语。
取消每词发音曾被示范的说明。
analyses: A they 指这些词，不是人类身份。
B told...Turkish 与 weren’t 揭示给参与者的说法非真实语种归属。
C 不可从给假词猜意思推出掌握真实语言。
D showed how to pronounce 仍成立；不把文中掩饰当本网站应对读者撒谎的指令。

vocabulary.meaning: 读出发音；发出某词的声音
vocabulary.context: 示范读音不等于这些词有真实土耳其语词义。
vocabulary.example: The instructor showed how to pronounce each unfamiliar string.
collocations: showed them how to pronounce each

questions.evidenceQuote: The findings from this research on word frequency are fascinating, but they are still correlational. That is, we cannot infer a causal effect between frequency and liking a word. So Zajonc designed an experiment in which participants were presented with nonsense words such as “iktitaf,” “afworbu,” and “saricik.” The experimenter told the participants that these were “Turkish” words (they weren’t) and showed them how to pronounce each.

questions.prompt: What were participants asked to do before judging the words' meanings?
questions.promptZh: 判断词的意思前，参与者被要求做什么？
options: Look up every item in a real Turkish dictionary.
Give a goodness rating before trying to pronounce any item.
Study verified dictionary definitions before any pronunciation.
Pronounce each word.
optionsZh: 在真实土耳其词典查每个词。
先评好坏，再尝试读出任何词。
发音前学习已核实的词典定义。
读出每个词。
analyses: A 不是查真实翻译。
B then pronounce 后 Afterward 才猜好坏，顺序不能颠倒。
C 当前为无意义词，无真实词典释义学习步骤。
D then asked to pronounce，Afterward 才猜好坏意味，顺序明确；读词不等于已知真词义。

vocabulary.meaning: 随后；在那之后
vocabulary.context: 连接读出词与接下来猜意义的步骤，不是先后任意。
vocabulary.example: Participants read the items aloud; afterward, they rated them.

questions.evidenceQuote: The participants were then asked to pronounce each word. Afterward, they were asked to guess the meaning of each “Turkish” word in terms of how good or bad they are. Some words were presented only once or twice, while others were presented ten or twenty-five times. That was how Zajonc manipulated familiarity.

questions.prompt: What kind of meaning judgement were participants asked to make?
questions.promptZh: 参与者被要求作哪种词义判断？
options: To guess how good or bad the supposed words were.
To give a verified dictionary translation from Turkish into English.
To identify which printed magazine each word had come from.
Report how often each item appeared in books of the 1920s and 1930s.
optionsZh: 猜这些所谓词的意思是好还是坏。
给出经核实土耳其语到英语词典翻译。
辨认每词来自哪本杂志。
报告每项在1920、1930年代书中出现次数。
analyses: A guess meaning...in terms of how good or bad 是情感效价判断，不是准确译词测验。
B 无意义词无该项真实词典答案。
C 书刊词频属早前研究，不能移给编造刺激。
D 是前面自然词频资料，不是当前假词的好坏猜测任务。

vocabulary.meaning: 从……角度；按某一维度
vocabulary.context: 这里限定 good/bad 情感判断，不是所有语言语义能力。
vocabulary.example: The responses were compared in terms of how positive they seemed.
collocations: in terms of how good or bad

questions.evidenceQuote: The participants were then asked to pronounce each word. Afterward, they were asked to guess the meaning of each “Turkish” word in terms of how good or bad they are. Some words were presented only once or twice, while others were presented ten or twenty-five times. That was how Zajonc manipulated familiarity.

questions.prompt: How did Zajonc manipulate familiarity in this task?
questions.promptZh: 这项任务中 Zajonc 怎样操纵熟悉度？
options: Change the positivity of each definition while keeping presentation counts identical.
By giving every word the identical exposure count.
By varying presentation frequency, with some words shown once or twice and others ten or twenty-five times.
By telling participants the true Turkish meaning of every item.
optionsZh: 保持呈现次数相同，只改变每词定义的正面程度。
给每个词相同曝光次数。
改变呈现频率：一些一两次，另一些十次或二十五次。
给每项真实土耳其词义。
analyses: A 实际操纵出现次数，不是给相同次数后改变真定义。
B counts 明确不同，不是同次数。
C Some...while others 的差别是 That was how 回指的操纵。
D 假词不是真土耳其词，且操纵的是次数而非真实释义；不把次数自动写成所有人的相同觉察。

vocabulary.meaning: 在实验中有意改变；操纵变量
vocabulary.context: 这里是调整刺激出现次数，不是操控真实人的思想或伪造数据。
vocabulary.example: The researchers manipulated exposure by varying the number of presentations.

questions.evidenceQuote: The participants were then asked to pronounce each word. Afterward, they were asked to guess the meaning of each “Turkish” word in terms of how good or bad they are. Some words were presented only once or twice, while others were presented ten or twenty-five times. That was how Zajonc manipulated familiarity.

questions.prompt: What new material was used to replicate the initial nonsense-word finding?
questions.promptZh: 复现初始无意义词发现时，用了什么新材料？
options: Marriage licences from Philadelphia only.
Dormitory floor plans instead of any visual symbols.
The same English pair good and better without any new material.
Chinese characters.
optionsZh: 只有费城结婚许可。
不用视觉符号而用宿舍平面图。
没有新材料，仅原英语 good/better。
汉字。
analyses: A 是别节不同数据。
B 当前没有改用宿舍图。
C then replicated...with Chinese characters 明确不同材料。
D 直接对应，后面照片又是下一实验；不能把用汉字写成参与者一定是中国人或全会中文。

vocabulary.meaning: 重复验证；以另一材料再现所述模式
vocabulary.context: 不等于机械复制字形，也不保证任何刺激、任何情境总同效。
vocabulary.example: The team replicated the pattern with a different set of images.

questions.evidenceQuote: He found that all twelve nonsense words were rated higher on goodness when presented more frequently than when presented less frequently. He then replicated this initial finding with Chinese characters. In the next experiment, Zajonc used photos of graduating Michigan State University seniors and replicated again that those same photos were better liked when presented more frequently to the participants than when they were presented less frequently.

questions.prompt: What does 'The story ... doesn’t stop here' prepare the reader for?
questions.promptZh: The story...doesn’t stop here 为后文做什么铺垫？
options: The retraction of every prior result as fabricated.
An extension from earlier laboratory examples to a real-classroom field experiment.
The claim that only nonsense words can ever be liked.
The end of the chapter before any further example.
optionsZh: 把此前全部结果撤回为编造。
从早前实验室例子延伸到真实课堂实地实验。
声称只有无意义词能受喜欢。
不给更多例子便结束本章。
analyses: A 继续不是撤回，也无 fabricated 声明。
B 下一句 field experiment...real college classroom 明确扩展。
C 已有汉字与照片，非仅假词。
D doesn’t stop 正与结束相反；不把故事一词误解成所有研究都为小说。

vocabulary.meaning: 不止于此；还有后续
vocabulary.context: 过渡标记，接更多证据而非宣布此前无效。
vocabulary.example: The argument doesn't stop here; another setting is examined next.

questions.evidenceQuote: The story of the mere exposure effect doesn’t stop here. Richard Moreland and Bob Zajonc ran a field experiment in a real college classroom. They selected four female research assistants who were rated as equally attractive to attend an introduction to psychology class with various degrees of frequency. One woman never attended the lecture, the second woman attended five times, the third woman attended ten times, and the fourth one attended fifteen times over the course of the semester.

questions.prompt: Where did Moreland and Zajonc conduct the field experiment described here?
questions.promptZh: 这里 Moreland 与 Zajonc 在哪里开展实地实验？
options: In a real college classroom.
Only in a language laboratory with no real students attending class.
At the Philadelphia marriage-licence office in 1931.
In Kepler's household during the seventeenth century.
optionsZh: 真实大学课堂。
仅无人真实上课的语言实验室。
1931费城结婚许可办公室。
十七世纪 Kepler 家里。
analyses: A real college classroom 与后文心理学导论课对应。
B 与真实课堂限定相反。
C 是前文不同研究。
D 历史故事不是现代课堂研究；不把 field experiment 当只要观察地址、不操纵任何条件的意思。

vocabulary.meaning: 实地实验；在真实生活环境进行的实验
vocabulary.context: 此处课堂里改变出席频率，区别早前实验室材料与单纯观察性记录。
vocabulary.example: A field experiment tested the idea during an ordinary course.

questions.evidenceQuote: The story of the mere exposure effect doesn’t stop here. Richard Moreland and Bob Zajonc ran a field experiment in a real college classroom. They selected four female research assistants who were rated as equally attractive to attend an introduction to psychology class with various degrees of frequency. One woman never attended the lecture, the second woman attended five times, the third woman attended ten times, and the fourth one attended fifteen times over the course of the semester.

questions.prompt: Who is described as dressed casually, according to this passage?
questions.promptZh: 据片段，谁被描述为穿便装？
options: All Dutch people who started cohabiting in 2004.
Only the lecturer, while no assistants attended.
The women instructed to enter the lecture hall and sit where students could see them.
Every student in all universities throughout the semester.
optionsZh: 2004开始同居的所有荷兰人。
只有讲师，且无助理出席。
被要求进讲堂并坐在学生可见处的女性。
整学期所有大学的每个学生。
analyses: A They 延续课堂女性助理，不是荷兰队列。
B enter...walk...sit 的行动主体不是仅讲师。
C They...all dressed casual 归属明确，但不能添加她们服装每处完全相同。
D all 限定这些行动者，不扩成所有大学学生；casual 也不是不在意实验。

vocabulary.meaning: 以日常随意的穿着方式；穿便装
vocabulary.context: fashion 在此为方式或风格，不表示最新流行或相同品牌。
vocabulary.example: The assistants were dressed in a casual fashion.

questions.evidenceQuote: They were instructed to enter the lecture hall, walk the same staircases, and sit in the same area, so that most students could see them. They were all dressed in a casual fashion.

questions.prompt: What does the paragraph say more exposure was associated with?
questions.promptZh: 段落说更多曝光还与什么相关？
options: Proven identical life histories for all participants.
Greater verified agreement on objective personality questionnaires.
Every student explicitly knowing all four women personally.
Greater perceived similarity.
optionsZh: 所有参与者完全相同的生活史已证实。
客观人格问卷上已核实的一致程度增加。
每个学生明确私人认识四名女性。
更强的主观相似感。
analyses: A perceived 不等于人生事实完全同。
B perceived similarities 是评分者的主观相似感，不是这里已核实客观人格真的变同。
C 下一句例说 nobody said knew，不支持全认识。
D associated with more perceived similarities 原文直接对应，保留主观评分与关联措辞。

vocabulary.meaning: 主观感到的相似之处；被认为的相似性
vocabulary.context: 区别客观身份、遗传、经历真正变同，也不等于互相认识。
vocabulary.example: The ratings reflected perceived similarities rather than verified shared histories.

questions.evidenceQuote: Likewise, more exposure was associated with more perceived similarities, as well. Interestingly, the mere exposure effect seems to happen without much awareness. For instance, when students were explicitly asked whether they knew these four women, nobody said yes. Very few people said they had seen them before.

questions.prompt: What did students say when explicitly asked whether they knew the four women?
questions.promptZh: 明确问是否认识四名女性时，学生怎么回答？
options: Every student said yes and named a friendship history.
Nobody said yes.
Exactly half said yes, with a verified contact list.
They all said they had never seen any face at any earlier moment.
optionsZh: 每人说认识并列友情历史。
无人回答认识。
恰一半说认识且有核实通讯录。
全说以前任何时刻从未见任何面孔。
analyses: A 与 nobody said yes 相反。
B 限定该次 knew 提问的回答，不把它改成客观从未被曝光。
C 无一半或通讯录数字。
D 下一句 Very few said seen before 与认识的问题不同，不可混为绝对从未见过或等同有意识认知。

vocabulary.meaning: 明确地；直接问明地
vocabulary.context: 修饰询问是否认识，不意味着学生已明确意识到曝光操纵。
vocabulary.example: The questionnaire explicitly asked whether they recognised the person.

questions.evidenceQuote: Likewise, more exposure was associated with more perceived similarities, as well. Interestingly, the mere exposure effect seems to happen without much awareness. For instance, when students were explicitly asked whether they knew these four women, nobody said yes. Very few people said they had seen them before.

questions.prompt: What relation is attributed to previous research in the target sentence?
questions.promptZh: 目标句把哪种关系归于此前研究？
options: Perceived similarity leads to attraction.
Attraction necessarily makes all people objectively identical.
Every chance meeting inevitably results in marriage.
Residential distance has been proved irrelevant to any encounter.
optionsZh: 主观相似感带来吸引。
吸引必使所有人客观相同。
每次偶遇必然导致婚姻。
住址距离已证明与任何接触无关。
analyses: A previous research...perceived similarity leads to attraction 明示方向和 perceived 限定。
B 倒置方向并将主观感受偷换成客观同一。
C attraction 不是每次婚姻的充分条件；全段机制总结不能作关系保证。
D 前文讨论邻近与接触，不是距离无关的结论；本题引用目标句，不提前计入其他未配句。

vocabulary.meaning: 被感知的；主观认为的
vocabulary.context: 区分评分者眼中的相似与客观已核实特征，不声称人的实际背景因曝光改变。
vocabulary.example: Perceived similarity may differ from objectively shared traits.

questions.evidenceQuote: Previous research already convincingly demonstrated that perceived similarity leads to attraction.
